content:
Two competing accounts of a death in federal custody are now on the record in Laredo. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said Tuesday that Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias received proper medical care while detained — but his family disputes that, and U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar is demanding answers the agency has not yet provided, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Andrade-Covarrubias, found unresponsive in his assigned bed around 9:48 a.m. Saturday, October 17, was pronounced dead at 10:10 a.m. The cause of death remains unknown pending an autopsy by the Webb County Medical Examiner’s Office, the Times reported.

ICE said in a statement Tuesday that he “received proper medical care while in custody and was seen by medical professionals,” and noted a documented medical history of diabetes, hypertension and anxiety. The agency described its general procedures — intake screenings within 12 hours of arrival, a full health assessment within 14 days, access to appointments and 24-hour emergency care — but did not address the family’s specific allegations about medication or individual requests for care.

His daughter, 29-year-old Estefani Andrade, told The Texas Tribune a starkly different story: her father had a heart condition and had been complaining to his family about health problems while detained; he had medication with him when he was detained but facility staff would not give it to him; he complained of a cough, trouble breathing and tightness in his chest; and when he sought help, medical staff ignored his concerns. She also disputed ICE’s account of his immigration history — the agency has said he obtained lawful permanent resident status fraudulently by failing to disclose a 2004 arrest for theft, while she said he did disclose his record and was approved.

Andrade-Covarrubias, a Dallas resident who painted apartments and townhomes and had three children, had been in immigration detention since June 26, when Customs and Border Protection arrested him at the Juarez-Lincoln Bridge. He was in removal proceedings, with an immigration hearing scheduled November 2, according to the Times.

Cuellar, who visited the Rio Grande Processing Center at 1001 San Rio Blvd. on Monday, said staff could not discuss the case because the death remains under investigation — so he submitted seven written questions to ICE, including whether Andrade-Covarrubias requested medical attention during the 72 hours before his death, what treatment and medications he received, and whether the facility followed its medical and emergency-response procedures. ICE had not publicly answered them as of publication. “Any death in federal custody is a serious matter, and we need to know what happened,” Cuellar said. “I will continue following up until we get the information we need.”

The Department of Homeland Security’s Office of Inspector General and ICE’s Office of Professional Responsibility were notified of the death, consistent with agency policy. He is the second person to die this year while detained by ICE in Laredo — Felix Alcorta-Rodriguez, 63, died June 19 after being found unresponsive at the Webb County Detention Center, the Times noted.

The questions now on the table are simple ones: did he ask for help in his final 72 hours, and what did the facility do? Until ICE answers Cuellar’s seven questions, the public is left with two irreconcilable stories — and a family in Dallas waiting for an autopsy.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, Webb Watch 956

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: ICE says detainee Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias got proper medical care before his Oct. 17 death; his daughter disputes that, and Rep. Henry Cuellar has submitted seven unanswered questions to the agency.
title: ICE Says Detainee Who Died in Laredo Got Proper Medical Care; Family Disputes It as Cuellar Demands Answers
